blockers: Unsupported claim: Method says 'A probe asking each model which study it was part of found no study context.' No probe job, raw output or result exists in exps/, harness/, results/ (grep for probe/study-context finds only incidental text). Isolation itself is implemented (harness/run_jobs.py: --setting-sources '', --strict-mcp-config, --tools '', empty cwd, fixed system prompt) and sampled C2/S1 prompts contain only problem + candidates + generic instructions, but the probe claim has no artifact.

Headline H1 reading rests on a gate not pre-registered. exps/c2_confirm/PREREGISTRATION.md requires gates 'per model and set' (solve rate in [0.2,0.8]); the 79-problem arXiv set failed (solve 0.05, AMENDMENTS 'Outcome') and is 'not interpreted'. The paper nonetheless interprets the union (103 problems, 'gate passed', solve 0.206 / 0.204 with a missing call counted unsolved, i.e. barely inside the band because 24 easy contest problems offset 79 failing ones) and the abstract says the penalty is 'concentrated in arXiv-derived problems', which is the set it declares uninterpretable. The union gate rule is not in the prereg.

Apples-to-oranges comparison reported without its caveat. paper/main.tex Screen section contrasts TP false-choice PICK 0.08 vs ISO-any 0.30; exps/screens/s1_lineup/SCREEN_NOTE.md states this 'favours single-choice formats by construction' (ISO-any over 3 calls can accept several candidates, PICK at most one). The paper omits that and invites a causal reading.

Gemma-2-2b is declared to 'carry no weight' under the study's rules, yet the competence paragraph says the post hoc split 'agrees with the large PICK effect of an outdated weak model' (exps/p1_lineup_math/results.txt: PICK-ISO n=29 because 18 of 80 PICK replies failed to parse, 10 of 40 SOLVE unparsed). It is used as supporting evidence after being excluded.
non_blocking: Scope statement 'Calls were made on 3 November 2026' is inaccurate: C2 amendments D2 and raw commit d116b6f show retries ran 4 Nov 00:48 UTC.

Undisclosed deviations in the paper: sonnet C2 arm cost 29.10 USD against a pre-registered 12 USD cap (C2 AMENDMENTS D3); one sonnet PICK call blocked by an API safeguard (D1) so sonnet H1 uses n=17, while the paper says 'Sonnet's confirmation has 24 problems'; sonnet gate parse rate is 0.896 but displays as 0.90 against a 0.90 threshold (c2_sonnet_isoparse), which reads as a pass; one haiku SOLVE call missing; the replication pools were rebuilt with MA_ALL_MODELS after the first lock was empty (banks/locked_ma/LOCK.md; paper says only that candidates come from all models).

S9 pre-registration says it 'uses screen split problems that haiku solved in a no-note call'; build.py (exps/screens/s9_peernote/build.py) runs all 60 problems (control accuracy 0.61), and the note's wrong answer is the cid-sorted first wrong candidate. Deviation not recorded in AMENDMENTS or the paper. S8 omitted the consultancy baseline (its own SCREEN_NOTE says so). S7 (haiku-sonnet phi) is in the v2 prereg but absent from the paper.
S5 attribution prompt gives the ground-truth answer to the attributor (SCREEN_NOTE); the paper does not say so.

CLI version 2.1.317 is sourced in results/claims.json from loop/STEER.md, not from any raw call record (raw JSON keys: id,result,rc,cost,model_used,usage,...), so it cannot be verified from artifacts. Adaptive thinking 'on by default' is not set by harness code; it is an unpinned CLI default (disclosed).

Provenance wording: paper says the author wrote 'rules and gates', but PROVENANCE.md says the agent wrote the preregistrations and chose benchmarks; 'pre-registered' means git commits by the same agent, not an external registry. Pools are locked with hashes (sha256 verified to match banks/locked_ma and exps/c2_confirm/pools.json; job prompts built from them).

Pools select first three distinct wrong answers by alphabetical model_name and drop unparsed answers; distinctness is by string, so equivalent answers can count as distinct. Disclosed only as 'not a random sample'.

Prompts do not reveal correctness: sampled ISO, PICK and FORCED lines in jobs_haiku.jsonl contain only problem, candidate text, 'Final answer', and a generic instruction; role/cid/gen labels live only in job ids and pools.json. Candidate text is a raw model output and could contain self-assessment, which is realistic.
